pr.body:
Changes:
- Initializes unified storage when the `ResourceServer` is created, instead of doing it inside the first gRPC call it receives. This was causing context cancelled errors since the index takes too long to build within the context of the gRPC call.
- Fixes trace propagation by passing span contexts down.
- Improves index build speed using finer grain locking when writing the index cache. We were locking the whole `BuildIndex` function, which was slowing things down when building many namespaces with high concurrency.

Notes for reviewer:
- Does anything else depend on initializing US lazily? What could this break?
pr.title: Unified Storage: Init at startup, fix traces, and speed up indexing

raw_findings.body: `Stop()` still sets `s.initErr = "service is stopping"` / `"service is stopped"`, but no RPC consults it anymore, so requests are executed against a cancelled watcher context and a stopped/closed backend instead of being rejected with a clear error; callers see backend-level errors or writes against a shutting-down store.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Requests arriving after shutdown are processed instead of failing fast, producing confusing downstream errors during shutdown.
raw_findings.impact: `Stop()` still sets `s.initErr = "service is stopping"` / `"service is stopped"`, but no RPC consults it anymore, so requests are executed against a cancelled watcher context and a stopped/closed backend instead of being rejected with a clear error; callers see backend-level errors or writes against a shutting-down store.
raw_findings.root_cause: The eager `s.Init(ctx)` in the constructor was treated as a full replacement for the per-RPC `Init` calls, but those calls also acted as the post-Stop request gate via `initErr`.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Keep a lightweight state check at the top of the RPC handlers (e.g. `if err := s.initErr; err != nil { return nil, err }` or a dedicated `stopped` flag/atomic) so post-Stop requests are still rejected, even though Init now happens in the constructor.
raw_findings.title: Removing per-RPC Init() guard lets requests run after Stop()
raw_findings.trigger: A client issues Create/Update/Delete/Read/List/Watch/Search after `server.Stop(ctx)` has run (graceful shutdown while in-flight or late requests are still arriving).

raw_findings.body: `bleveBackend.TotalDocs()` iterates `b.cache` without taking `cacheMu`, so a concurrent map write from BuildIndex can trigger Go's fatal "concurrent map read and map write" runtime crash of the storage server during startup.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Process aborts with a Go runtime map race fatal error; no recovery is possible.
raw_findings.impact: `bleveBackend.TotalDocs()` iterates `b.cache` without taking `cacheMu`, so a concurrent map write from BuildIndex can trigger Go's fatal "concurrent map read and map write" runtime crash of the storage server during startup.
raw_findings.root_cause: A new unsynchronized read of the bleve index cache was introduced at a point where the event-handling goroutine can already be mutating that cache under the newly narrowed `cacheMu` write lock.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Either take `b.cacheMu.RLock()` around the `b.cache` iteration in `bleveBackend.TotalDocs()`, or compute/log the total document count before starting the watch goroutine.
raw_findings.title: New TotalDocs() call races with concurrent bleve cache writes from the watch goroutine
raw_findings.trigger: The watch goroutine started a few lines above (`go func() { ... s.handleEvent(watchctx, v) }()`) receives an event for a not-yet-cached namespace/resource and builds an index (`bleveBackend.BuildIndex` writes `b.cache[key] = idx`) at the same moment `init` logs and calls `s.search.TotalDocs()`.

raw_findings.body: The `cancel` obtained from `context.WithCancel` at construction is never invoked and `Stop()` can never be called on the discarded server, so the derived context and any goroutines/watchers already started by the partially completed init (e.g. the search watch goroutine) are leaked for the process lifetime.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Resource/goroutine leak on failed startup, invisible until memory or watcher accumulation shows up.
raw_findings.impact: The `cancel` obtained from `context.WithCancel` at construction is never invoked and `Stop()` can never be called on the discarded server, so the derived context and any goroutines/watchers already started by the partially completed init (e.g. the search watch goroutine) are leaked for the process lifetime.
raw_findings.root_cause: Eager initialization was added after the cancelable context/goroutine setup without adding the corresponding cleanup on the new error return path.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: On the Init error path, call `cancel()` (and optionally `s.lifecycle.Stop`) before returning the error.
raw_findings.title: NewResourceServer leaks the cancelable server context when eager Init fails
raw_findings.trigger: Startup where `lifecycle.Init` or `search.init` fails (e.g. DB not reachable, index directory unwritable), so the constructor returns an error.

raw_findings.body: Every startup failure emits the identical error log line twice, making log-based alerting and debugging noisier and suggesting two distinct failures.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Duplicated diagnostics reduce log signal quality.
raw_findings.impact: Every startup failure emits the identical error log line twice, making log-based alerting and debugging noisier and suggesting two distinct failures.
raw_findings.root_cause: The new eager-init call site repeats the logging that `Init` already performs for the same error.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Drop the log call here and just `return nil, err`, relying on the existing log inside `Init`.
raw_findings.title: Duplicate error log for init failure in NewResourceServer
raw_findings.trigger: Any init failure: `server.Init` already logs `s.log.Error("error initializing resource server", "error", s.initErr)` inside `once.Do` before returning.

raw_findings.body: Regressions in the newly eager `NewResourceServer`/`Init` startup path on postgres go undetected, and the untracked TODO has no issue reference so the gap is unlikely to be closed.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Integration test reports pass while providing no coverage for postgres storage-server startup.
raw_findings.impact: Regressions in the newly eager `NewResourceServer`/`Init` startup path on postgres go undetected, and the untracked TODO has no issue reference so the gap is unlikely to be closed.
raw_findings.root_cause: A blanket postgres skip was added instead of addressing the failure the eager-initialization change surfaced in Drone.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Investigate and fix the postgres failure (likely startup timing after the eager init change) or, at minimum, reference a tracking issue in the TODO/skip message so the skipped coverage is auditable.
raw_findings.title: Postgres coverage silently dropped for storage-server integration test
raw_findings.trigger: CI runs with `GRAFANA_TEST_DB=postgres`; the only remaining supported backend for this test is MySQL, so the storage-server startup path (which this PR changes to initialize unified storage eagerly) is never exercised on postgres.

finding.verifier_reason: The patch removes per-RPC Init() calls, but Stop() still sets s.initErr which is checked by Init(). finding.title: New TotalDocs() call races with concurrent bleve cache writes from the watch goroutine
finding.trigger: The watch goroutine started a few lines above (`go func() { ... s.handleEvent(watchctx, v) }()`) receives an event for a not-yet-cached namespace/resource and builds an index (`bleveBackend.BuildIndex` writes `b.cache[key] = idx`) at the same moment `init` logs and calls `s.search.TotalDocs()`.
finding.verifier_reason: The candidate claims TotalDocs() races with BuildIndex writing to b.cache. However, examining bleve.go lines 137-139, BuildIndex takes cacheMu.Lock() before writing to cache. TotalDocs() at line 144-153 iterates b.cache without locking, but the watch goroutine started at line 207 calls handleEvent which eventually may call BuildIndex. The race window exists but the claim that 'the watch goroutine...builds an index' during TotalDocs is speculative - handleEvent doesn't directly call BuildIndex for new namespaces during normal event handling. The timing scenario described is unlikely.
